messages.subject: interactive filtering in leaves
parts:
Hi, 

I have some problems with interactive filtering of my dataset for two different variables in two different layers.
If I apply the filters step by step in the main tree it works fine, but it implicates that the first filter dominates the second.
If I instead want to apply the filters independently in two different leaves, I get "Error in match(x, table, nomatch = 0L) :  'match' requires vector arguments"

Would be great if anyone could help out.

Best, Florian

Here's my minimal example with the diamonds dataset from ggplot2


library("dplyr")
library("ggplot2")
library("ggvis")
library("shiny")

set.seed(123)
dslice <- tbl_df(diamonds %>% slice(sample(1:dim(diamonds)[1],50)) %>% arrange(price))

## input filters in main chain
dslice %>%
   ggvis(~carat, ~depth) %>% 
   filter(cut %in% eval(input_checkboxgroup(
      c(levels(diamonds$cut)), 
      selected = c(levels(diamonds$cut)), 
      label="cut"))) %>% 
   layer_points(fill = ~clarity, size := 50, opacity := 0.5) %>%
   filter(price > eval(input_slider(
      min = 0, 
      max = max(dslice$price), 
      value = 5000, 
      step = 100, 
      label = "price"))) %>%
   layer_points(fill := "black", size = ~price, shape := "cross")

## input filters in leaves
ggvis(data=NULL, ~carat, ~depth) %>%
   layer_points(fill = ~clarity, size := 50, opacity := 0.5, data = dslice %>%
                   filter(cut %in% eval(input_checkboxgroup(
                      c(levels(diamonds$cut)), 
                      selected = c(levels(diamonds$cut)), 
                      label="cut")))) %>%
   layer_points(fill := "black", size = ~price, shape := "cross", data = dslice %>%
                   filter(price > eval(input_slider(
                      min = 0, 
                      max = max(dslice$price), 
                      value = 5000, 
                      step = 100, 
                      label = "price"))))

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: interactive filtering in leaves
parts:
Hi Florian,

The problem is that in the first case you're running filter.ggvis and
in the second your running filter.data.frame. filter.ggvis
understands reactivity, and how to deal with sliders etc, but
filter.data.frame does not. If you wanted to implement the second
option, I think you'd need to use shiny explicitly.

Hadley
